analysis.title: International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 20, 2026)
key_insights: Global equities sold off broadly after a short-lived tech relief rally. Defensives were not spared, with India the exception. Client feedback points to continued risk unwind and limited appetite to add exposure.

AI and tech are at the center of the selloff. The drivers named are expanding China export-control concerns and growing cyber threats on reports of customer data leaks. The VIX spiked to levels last seen in March.

Korea and Taiwan were the worst hit in APAC. Taiwan likely has further to go because its retail de-leverage is still underway and it is held more by foreigners than Korea, where de-risking happened earlier.

US Electricals research sees negative implications from China tech earnings for AI capex-related names. Tencent called for peak capex in 2027, and Alibaba cash flow should turn positive in 2H28 as spending moderates.
The selloff is broadening beyond tech, weighed by risks of US strikes on Iran and increasingly hawkish Fed speak.
Dispersion is normalizing. In Q3 over 40% of SPX constituents had a negative 3m rolling beta to the index, and JPM's tracker has now broken below 20% as risk-off extends across the index.
US Economics outlook work flags capex and the wealth effect as the two key points, both set to moderate next year.
Next week's catalysts: Global S&P PMIs, Taiwan IP, US PCE, Fed Beige Book, ECB October minutes and the BOK rate decision.

EMEA Metals & Mining: some copper-exposed miners now trade below their pre-US/Iran conflict (27 Feb) 2027E EV/EBITDA multiples, while iron-ore-dominant names trade at or above Feb 2026 multiples. JPM sees downside risks as elevated and recommends staying selective.

Japan lifers' FX-denominated portfolios are mostly corporate bonds (48%) and other foreign securities (27%), with government bonds at 16%. JPM sees high hurdles for large-scale repatriation. Lifers can respond to yen appreciation risk by raising hedge ratios rather than selling foreign bonds.

Market Intelligence is tactically bullish on global equities. Broadening and international (ex-US) have led over the past month on ex-AI rotation and expectations of a flatter geopolitical curve in 2027 after the US midterms.
EU outperformance is supported by earnings (~13% median YoY EPS growth in Q3, same as the US) and positioning. EU vs US positioning is now back to neutral after relative extreme lows.

JPM expects a tactical tech bounce led by US/APAC semis and AI thematics. The case rests on extreme tech selloff readings (speed of unwind, six straight weeks of HF selling in US semis, QQQ short interest, bearish retail sentiment) and valuations that already imply imminent EPS cuts.

The bounce is described as technical and short-term, and less V-shaped than in H1. Buyside capex expectations show signs of peaking, and the rotation out of AI may extend on funding pressures, questions over AI ARR trends and policy uncertainty.

Positioning Intelligence: HF selling in US semis extended to a sixth consecutive week, the longest streak on record. Global HF net exposure is down 67% from its year-to-date high, the lowest since September 2025.

A semis rebound may need stabilization and renewed HF buying. Global semis exposure is still around the 80th percentile since 2018, and HF positioning z-score trails relative-returns z-score, so history suggests a rebound may not be robust.
HF performance gained about 1.5% over five days and is roughly flat month to date globally. Europe is up 1.7% MTD and Asia is down 2%.
Japan was broadly sold. HFs sold all 11 sectors over the month, and combined Japan positioning has fallen to the 24th percentile since 2015.

vol_and_positioning: The VIX spiked to levels seen in March.
HF net flows in US semis were below -3z for the second week in a row, and HF selling extended to a sixth consecutive week, the longest streak on record.
Global HF net exposure is down 67% from its year-to-date high, the lowest since September 2025. The global long/short ratio fell from 4.4x to 2.1x.
Combined 6m positioning plus price z-score for semis is near -3z, which could produce a bounce like the one after the late-July momentum reduction.
Global semis exposure is still around the 80th percentile versus data since 2018.
After near -2z de-grossing on Monday, flows calmed Tuesday to Thursday. Thursday was the most positive global re-gross day in about a month.
HF gross leverage fell 4% week over week and net leverage was broadly unchanged. The US Tactical Positioning Monitor is at the 20th percentile since 2015.
European flows rose +1.5z relative to US flows over 1-3 months, bringing relative EU positioning back to neutral.
Japan HF flows were -1.4z WoW and -2.3z MoM. Combined Japan positioning is at the 24th percentile since 2015, with a roughly -2z 4-week change.
QQQ short interest and retail sentiment toward semis are described as extreme or very low.
Taiwan's retail de-leverage is still underway.
geopolitical: Risks of US strikes on Iran are growing and weigh on the macro narrative.
Expanding China export-control concerns are weighing on AI and tech sentiment.
JPM sees geopolitical resolution as not in the cards near term.
The US/Iran conflict date of 27 Feb is used as a reference point for miners' multiples.
Catalyst calendar: Trump, Xi and Putin meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit (19/11). EU foreign ministers discuss RU/UA and ME. An EU-UK summit is held in Brussels on 20/11.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech selloff screens extreme on speed of unwind, six straight weeks of HF selling in US semis, QQQ short interest and bearish retail sentiment. Valuations already imply imminent EPS cuts, and classic cycle-peak signals such as inventory builds or shortening lead times are absent.
tension_points.bear_case: The bounce is technical and short-term and less V-shaped than in H1. Buyside capex expectations show signs of peaking, and the rotation out of AI may extend on funding pressures, questions over AI ARR trends and policy uncertainty.
tension_points.what_invalidates: JPM says the semis rebound may not be robust unless HF positioning z-score starts to catch up with relative-returns z-score, i.e. HFs get more bullish.
